limitations: Live interactive application workflows were not verified in this round.
Document revisions are immutable scene checkpoints and do not provide an editable or replayable general feature timeline, arbitrary operation reorder/insert, dependency graph, branch, or merge.

The bounded parametric chain supports named inputs and suppression of its through-hole, blind-hole, pattern, chamfer, and downstream fillet where supported. The 2D point/segment solver persists polygon sketch constraints and supports dimension/anchor edits after reopening, but the UI cannot yet add non-fixed geometric constraints or arcs/splines. Blind holes cannot yet be patterned; chamfer must precede fillet in the supported blend order.

Surface faces and shells persist as scene bodies; connected open-shell sewing, solid-guided trim and splitting of a face or sewn multi-face shell, stitch-to-solid, and thickening are implemented and regression-tested. Open-shell sewing requires one connected result and rejects incomplete face retention; solid-guided splitting checks area conservation and stores each fragment separately. Arbitrary free-form split/merge, preview, editable surface history, and live UI verification remain outstanding. Planar single-face thickening uses extrusion; curved or multi-face bodies depend on OCCT offset thickening and may reject difficult self-intersecting cases.

Mesh repair is integrated into STL and OBJ intake; only strictly convex planar holes up to 64 boundary edges can be filled. Open manifold meshes can be imported as faceted surface bodies; non-manifold meshes and native triangle editing remain unsupported.
Automated drawing readiness checks do not certify ISO or ASME compliance.
Drawing source status tracks geometry and BOM/material revisions, but SVG and PDF exports remain point-in-time snapshots.

Assembly occurrence patterns create static occurrences rather than a live associative feature; counts are capped at 100, circular patterns rotate about world Z, and jointed subassemblies must be unlinked before patterning.

The interactive parametric foundation includes bounded rectangle/extrusion histories and constrained trapezoid/triangle/vertex-defined polygon extrusions whose point/segment constraints persist and can be edited after reopening. Non-fixed constraint creation remains unavailable in the UI.

Folded sheet-metal inputs can be saved and edited with an undoable rebuild; direct geometry edits make the definition stale/read-only. DXF export develops the saved input definition using one selected K-factor, but files are snapshots without reliefs or automatic refresh. Bodies use sampled facets; springback and tool compensation are not modeled.
